comparison: Both evaluate the genome-wide screening data (C22-C24). OpenEval finds the screening methodology and statistical analysis sufficient (SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers question the breadth of hits and absence of expected proteins like Ypt proteins and Imh1 (UNCERTAIN), indicating concerns about completeness or interpretation.

Both address sphingolipid intermediate accumulation (C2, C29-C34). OpenEval finds the lipidomic mass spectrometry data comprehensive and statistically significant (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but express uncertainty about the mechanistic explanation for sphingolipid mislocalization and whether changes result directly from trafficking defects (UNCERTAIN). Note: peer result also includes C35 which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

Both evaluate growth assay sensitivity data (C25-C28). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree these data are supported, with peer reviewers requesting extension to other GARP subunits rather than questioning the presented findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address myriocin rescue and sphingolipid turnover kinetics (C6, C36-C38). OpenEval finds the time-course data and growth assays supportive (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers accept the findings as 'surprising' and focus on extending rather than questioning them (SUPPORTED). Both agree on support.

Both evaluate sterol accumulation phenotypes. OpenEval addresses C3, C44-C47 with filipin and lipidomic data (SUPPORTED), while peer result R5 includes these claims plus C48-C49. Peer reviewers request critical experiments (myriocin rescue of sterol phenotype, simvastatin rescue of sphingolipid phenotype) to determine whether sterol changes are primary or secondary (UNCERTAIN), showing disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

OpenEval R6 addresses vacuolar morphology and NBD-sphingosine localization (C39-C41) as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 covers broader vacuolar dysfunction including C4, C39-C43, also rating as SUPPORTED. Both accept the lysosomal/vacuolar dysfunction data, with peer reviewers focusing on mechanistic questions rather than questioning the observations.

OpenEval R7 addresses zinc homeostasis and proteomic changes (C4, C42-C43) as SUPPORTED. This overlaps with peer R6 which covers broader vacuolar dysfunction (C4, C39-C43). Both find the data supported, though peer reviewers raise mechanistic questions about how GARP deficiency leads to these phenotypes.

Both evaluate the human disease mutation Q624R in yeast (C5, C51-C56, C86). OpenEval finds the yeast model data well-characterized and supportive of intermediate phenotype (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers express uncertainty about disease relevance, stating yeast studies are insufficient and requesting analysis in human cell lines (UNCERTAIN). Clear disagreement on adequacy of yeast model for disease claims.

OpenEval R11 addresses mammalian cell sterol and LAMP-1 phenotypes (C57-C60) as SUPPORTED but notes knockdown efficiency documentation needed. Peer R8 covers both sterol and sphingolipid phenotypes in mammalian cells (C57-C64), rating as SUPPORTED but requesting better disease models. Both accept HeLa data but note limitations.

OpenEval R12 addresses mammalian cell sphingolipid changes (C61-C64) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 includes these claims in broader mammalian cell evaluation (C57-C64), also SUPPORTED. Both accept the lipidomic data showing conservation from yeast to mammalian cells.

Both evaluate patient fibroblast data (C65-C66). OpenEval finds the sphingolipid imbalances and myriocin correction in patient cells strongly supportive (SUPPORTED), though notes sample size clarity needed. Peer reviewers accept the patient data (SUPPORTED) and focus on requesting additional experiments in human models. Both agree on support. Note: OpenEval R13 also includes C87 which peer reviewers address in R11.

Both address mechanistic models of lipid trafficking and rerouting. OpenEval R15 covers C67-C69, C78, C82 as SUPPORTED but notes direct trafficking experiments would strengthen conclusions. Peer R10 includes overlapping claims (C67, C69-C73, C78, C81-C82) but rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating authors have not provided adequate mechanistic explanation. Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence for proposed mechanism.

Both evaluate therapeutic implications (C92-C93). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis requires validation in disease-relevant models (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers similarly express uncertainty, stating therapeutic relevance is 'not yet clear' and requires better disease models (UNCERTAIN). Both agree on uncertainty.

Both address background literature and established knowledge (C1, C8-C21, C50, C74-C77, C83-C85, C88-C91). OpenEval and peer reviewers both treat these as SUPPORTED contextual claims from prior literature rather than novel findings requiring evaluation. Complete agreement.

OpenEval R9 addresses genetic interaction data for sterol homeostasis (C48-C49) as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes these claims within broader sterol phenotype evaluation (C3, C44-C49) rated as UNCERTAIN due to questions about primary vs. secondary defects. Partial overlap with different emphasis.

OpenEval R5 addresses Orm1 hyperphosphorylation (C35) and TORC2 pathway inference (C73) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C35 within sphingolipid accumulation evaluation (C2, C29-C35) rated as UNCERTAIN due to mechanistic questions. Partial overlap on C35 with different overall assessments.

OpenEval R20 addresses alternative mechanism speculation (C70-C71) as explicitly UNCERTAIN with no experimental evidence. Peer R10 includes these claims within broader mechanistic uncertainty (C67, C69-C73, C78, C81-C82). Both recognize these as speculative, though peer reviewers frame within larger mechanistic concerns.

OpenEval R16 addresses long-chain base toxicity mechanism (C72, C74-C76) as UNCERTAIN, noting reliance on citations rather than direct experimental evidence. Peer R12 includes C74-C76 among background literature claims rated as SUPPORTED. Disagreement stems from OpenEval treating these as mechanistic claims requiring validation vs. peer reviewers treating as established background knowledge.

OpenEval R17 addresses sterol accumulation and sphingolipid-sterol crosstalk (C79-C81) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanism remains speculative. Peer R10 includes C81 within broader mechanistic uncertainty. Minimal overlap with C81, different scope of evaluation.

OpenEval R14 addresses the central conclusion about sphingolipid imbalance as disease mechanism (C7) as SUPPORTED by comprehensive evidence. Peer R12 includes C7 among background/contextual claims. Minimal overlap; OpenEval treats C7 as the main novel conclusion while peer reviewers may categorize it differently.

OpenEval R5 includes TORC2 pathway inference (C73) as reasonable but not directly measured. Peer R10 includes C73 within mechanistic uncertainty about sphingolipid mislocalization. Both recognize C73 as inferential, minimal direct overlap.

OpenEval R13 includes C87 (myriocin correction in patient cells) as SUPPORTED. Peer R11 includes C87 within therapeutic implications rated as UNCERTAIN. Disagreement on whether patient cell rescue data adequately supports therapeutic potential.
OpenEval R16 includes C72 (long-chain base toxicity) as UNCERTAIN inference. Peer R10 includes C72 within broader mechanistic uncertainty. Both recognize uncertainty, minimal overlap in scope.

OpenEval R17 addresses sterol accumulation (C79) with filipin data. Peer R5 requests myriocin rescue of sterol phenotype to clarify primary vs. secondary defects. Related concerns about sterol phenotype interpretation but no direct claim overlap in the pairing.
